title: Lego Sensor Activities
description: I programmed Lego Mindstorms robots to complete three sensor-specific tasks, exploring the capabilities of the distance, touch, gyroscope, and color sensors, collaborating within a group to help each other complete the tasks.

timeline.heading: Initial Build
timeline.description: Since this project was mainly code-oriented, we decided to make the robot fairly basic. We opted to have 2 wheels and a rolling ball in the front to allow the robot to turn easily. We placed a touch sensor in the front, a color sensor pointing towards the ground, and a range sensor facing the side. The gyroscope was built in the brick.. This configuration worked well for most of the tasks, but if a sensor needs to be moved, then it could easily be removed and placed elsewhere.

timeline.heading: Task 1 - Range Sensor
timeline.description:
My first task required me to use a range sensor to drive along 3 lines of tape that changes distance from the wall every 3 feet.

I found coding this part the hardest out of the three as the robot would often glitch like going around in circles unexpectedly. Also, using the range sensor in this sense was buggy since whenever the robot would turn, the sensor would turn along it, causing the sensor to read out a distance bigger than the distance the robot was from the wall due to Pythagoras' theorem. I fixed this by making the robot face the wall at a small angle to ensure the sensor reading are as accurate as possible.

My code has 3 forever loops that check if the robot is close or far away from the wall, depending on the distance of the wall at that loop. If it is too close, the robot moves away from the wall, else it moves towards the wall.

timeline.heading: Task 2 - Gyroscope
timeline.description:
My second task required the robot to drive straight, even with outside influence trying to get the robot off course using the Gyroscope sensor.

This task was pretty simple as my code only checks the robot's yaw. If it's less than -1, it moves to the right, while if it's greater than 1, it moves to the left.

timeline.heading: Task 3 - Touch Sensor
timeline.description:
Task 3 required me to use the touch sensor to make a robot move straight until it hit a barrier. If it does, then it should turn and avoid that barrier.

This task was the simplest of the three tasks. My code constantly checks if the button is pressed. If it is, then it turns right to avoid the wall.

timeline.heading: Final Thoughts
timeline.description: Throughout this project, I developed many skills like problem solving, persistence, and communication with my team. I also gained more experience with code and the Lego Mindstorm coding language. In future projects, I would put the range sensor on a separate motor so the range sensor turns to face the wall directly, giving more accurate results. Overall, I have learned a lot about sensors from this and I think these skills will be very useful in future projects.
